steps.text: Preheat oven to 475 degrees F (245 degrees C).
Place the cubed potatoes, water, lemon juice, vegetable oil, and olive oil in a 12x18-inch baking dish or roasting pan. Season with oregano, salt, pepper, and garlic.

Roast, uncovered, in the preheated oven until the potatoes are tender and golden brown and the water has evaporated about 1 1/2 hours. Stir the potatoes every 20 minutes as they bake, adding more water as necessary to prevent sticking. Allow the water to evaporate during the final 15 to 20 minutes of cooking, but be careful that the potatoes do not burn. Stir in the chopped fresh parsley, and serve.

review.reviewBody: Did not make exactly as directed: subbed chicken stock for water. Why not add a little more flavour, unless going vegetarian? subbed olive oil for vegetable oil. increased oregano slightly. Let's just say that I eyeballed my measurements :). Amazing recipe: and I've passed it on to my friends. Tangy, fresh flavour. Kept me coming back for more! This is a keeper. Thank you for submitting this. ***edited to add: If you use a stock that isn't homemade, don't use the amount of salt noted in the recipe; it will be overly salty.

Turned out great once I made some changes. I only used olive oil and less of it (just enough to cover bottom of pan and little more) and I used 2 cups veggie broth instead of water and no salt. When I stirred part way through, I sprayed the tops with olive oil spray to keep it from drying out - I didn't see a need to add any water since I used more broth. Really a delicious recipe!

I made this low fat and it was still DELICIOUS and as good as our local Greek Restaurant. Since I used 5 lbs of potatoes, I used 3 Tbs of olive oil only. I used 4+c of water, 6 cloves of garlic and kept the seasonings the same as listed. I threw in an onion. Later it is good by adding steamed frozen mixed peppers and/or green beans or any vegetable.

I think I go against the popular opinion but I wasn't a big fan. I thought the lemon flavor was over powering and the potatoes were a bit mushy. I think I would try it again but just toss them with a small amount of olive oil and use about 1/2 a lemon squeezed over the cubed potatoes (no water). The cooking time would be cut in half too. I'll give it another try with a few tweaks.

I took the advice to substitute chicken broth for water. Otherwise, I followed the recipe exactly. As the potatoes baked, the fragrance filled the house and made waiting almost unendurable! Served with beef sausages. DH was very pleased and went for seconds. He wants this again anytime he can get it. Thank you for the recipe.

I've made this recipe many times now, and haven't changed a thing, which is unusual for me. Just be careful in the last 15 to 20 minutes. I always have to add more water, but you need to time it to be fairly dry toward the end. some potatoes may kind of start disintegrating on you if you stir them at the end too! Kudos to the chef who posted this.
Unbelievably delicious. The best i've ever made. Used chicken broth, and baked at a lower 400F for 1 1/2 hours. Potatoes were succulent!

Delicious! I was short on time so I made sure to cut my potatoes into fairly small chunks to speed up the cooking process. The only change I made was to add chicken broth instead of water. Topped with feta before serving. We loved them, thank you! :)

Thanks for a fabulous recipe. Made nearly as directed except didn't peel the red potatoes, must have cut smaller chunks of potatoes as mine were done in much less time, tripled the garlic, and used all olive oil. Everyone had seconds--even my "picky" niece who then took leftover potatoes for lunch the next day. Believe me there is no more resounding endorsement than that. The picture looked like it had feta sprinkled on top, but the recipe did not include. I'll try that next time as I think that would be really good. I will also use even more garlic next time. And next time will be both soon and often.

I've been looking for a great greek potato recipe for a while, and this is the BEST. I followed some of the suggestions from other reviews (added chicken stock and just used olive oil)... These potatoes came out better than any I've ever had at a greek restaurant.

Awesome potatoes.

This tasted great, wife loved it. However, mine turned out a little mushy. The potatoes kinda broke up. Had to broil them to brown the tops and get rid of some the liquid. Will make again, but maybe cut back on liquid a little.

If you double the recipe and the liquids, it does not boil off in the oven. I’ve waited the full 90 minutes and the potatoes are literally swimming in liquid.i need to remember this next time. I omit the salt and use vegetable bouillon in the water. Love this recipe when it turns out.
These were delicious! I eat them for dinner when I make them then, I love them cold out of the fridge the next day! They take a long time to cook so prepare ahead. Well worth the effort tho!
This was so simple to make and really delicious. The only thing I changed was adding in feta cheese towards the end of the cooking time. Will definitely make this again, the whole family loved it.
I substituted chicken broth for water as I was doing lemon chicken as the meat dish, but followed everything else. We had the leftovers for lunches the next day. Will definitely be making this again
Made this recipe more than once without any changes and we really enjoyed it.
Very good, but a bit too much lemon for my liking. Will make again with less lemon.
I have made this dish 4 times now and my family BEGS FOR IT. I make it as the recipe says, although the time is usually under an hour not and hour and a half.
Only quartered my potatoes and kept the skin. These came out great! Added some broccoli there at the end. Probably the best potato I have ever tasted.
My kids loved them, made extra and there were no leftovers.
